newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds down at short-end, improvement seen.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds down at short-end, improvement seen.

text.p: Irish bonds were weaker at the short end of the curve at the end of a busy day's trade on Tuesday but dealers said they expected to see a big improvement in this area tomorrow.
Dealers said the short end of the market would be helped by the release of better-than-expected end-November Exchequer Returns late on Tuesday.

Ireland's end-November Exchequer Returns showed a 153 million punt surplus compared with a cumulative exchequer borrowing requirement of 504 million punts for the same period last year, the Department of Finance said.
"They were very good numbers, much better than had been expected. We expected a surplus of around 75 million punts," one dealer said.

"The figures came out so late in the day the market has not had a chance to react to them yet. But I would expect these figures to help the short end tomorrow morning, making it attractive to buyers," the dealer added.

By 1735 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had eased 10 pence from Monday's close at 102.60 to yield 5.78 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 15 pence from the close at 110.60 to yield 6.38 percent.
Dealers said the domestic market had come under pressure at the short end on Tuesday for two reasons.

"First of all, there was a lot of nervousness in the market as the Irish pound continued to trade at below parity against sterling. The Irish pound rose to above parity late in the day and that too should help bonds," one dealer said.
"Secondly, there was a fear that the credit numbers due out on Thursday could actually be quite bad. People mightn't be so pessimistic now after today's figures," the dealer added.
Market analysts said a figure of between 13.5 and 14.0 percent was expected in the end-October banking statistics due out of the Central Bank on Thursday.
